criterionFindings.criterion: The preparation route requires a verified SessionActor (server-side authority; no client-supplied authority assertion or bearer capability in a request body) and binds an exact intent revision/hash

limitations: The extraction check is static and structural under a deliberately narrow bounded model (top-level exported consumers, one protected computation per proposal, removable trailing subject parameter or single-field props, declared callers); ambient shims declare externals data-only, so external behaviour is neither interpreted nor executed. Equivalence beyond the bounded model is not claimed anywhere and returns explicit not_supported.

Runtime preservation and integration execution of the proposed private diff remain pending gates for M4.3 after M5.2/M5.3 (real isolated runner); nothing in this review verifies them, and no isolated-runner or real-VM gate is claimed.

The extraction adapter is currently consumed only by the analysis partition suites; it is not yet wired into the private API or a persistence store (M4.1 concern recorded by the worker). The proposalHash is content-addressed for future approval binding, not yet an accepted release artifact.
Deterministic UUIDs are hash-derived PROPOSAL identifiers only; they are not task reservations, approvals, payments or published tasks (disclosed in the draft).

The demo declared-target source maps only the six synthetic demo goals to fixed synthetic private-shop paths; any other goal yields explicit missing_evidence. No real customer data, credentials or private runtime logs were used.

The preparation route is currently exercised by in-process/injected-transport tests (fastify inject with a trusted handler stub); the full HTTP journey through the canonical runtime is exercised by the e2e intent suite for the intent routes, and the coordinator's sweep recorded a rebuilt canonical runtime including the preparations wiring.
M2.2/M3.1 prerequisite independent reviews remain open (no accepted handoff files yet); this review covers the M3.2 revision under the sequential fallback and does not close prerequisite gates.
No secrets, prompts or real private fixture contents appear in this report; all observations use synthetic accounts and synthetic fixture data.
